transcript: Just got back from seeing Jack Little Pill on tour, and I think I liked it better the second time. I originally saw the show in 2019 on Broadway, and I had mixed feelings about it then. And then all the controversy happened surrounding some of the aspects of it, specifically the character of Joe and whether or not the character was written to be non binary. They did some rewrites to it. They cast a non binary performer as Joe for the tour. Course, Heidi Blick and stuff decide to do the tour, and I freaking love Heidi Blick and stuff. So I was like, Okay, I'll go see it again. And I think ultimately, the show worked better for me. I still had some of the same issues. For me personally, the thing that doesn't work the most with the show is the fact that there's just. There's too many storylines that are all, like, stuff together in this musical. It almost feels like there's 3 really good musicals, and then one musical that I. I probably wouldn't really want to see, but is also in there, and they're all woven together in this one show. And sometimes it works and sometimes it doesn't. Like, I think that there are parts of Bella and MJ stories that overlap really nicely because of everything else going on. I feel like Bella story kind of gets a little under baked. Same with the love triangle that is here. That feels Like, another musical entirely. Right? Like, I think that there's a lot of really interesting conversations that could be had and are kind of alluded to in that love triangle in terms of sexuality and gender. But because of everything else going on the show, especially a character like Phoenix kind of feels under baked. But, gosh, when this show is good, it is really good. There are 3 songs back to back to back and act 2. I call them the trifecta. If you've seen the show, you know exactly what I'm talking about. On their own, each of those 3 songs is such an incredible performance. Um, the. The performers that sing those songs are fantastic. The dancers in those songs are fantastic. Transitions between those songs is kind of clunky, but again, that goes back to too many ingredients in one pot, you know? Now, I've talked before about how I don't feel like this is a very strong book, and a lot of that is because it tries to cram too much in. But upon rewatch, some of these book scenes are, like, genuinely funny. Like, the book scenes on their own, when they don't have songs on them, are really good. I feel like Diablo Cody biggest struggle was trying to fit in all of the songs. And when. When you take that out, there's. There's a pretty decent play in here from a direct ring standpoint. I also feel like the ensemble is kind Of overused. And I'm very conflicted and even saying that because I think the ensemble is super talented, and when they're used well, it's incredibly powerful. But there are just some moments, specifically even just the opening prologue right before we start on the first scene, where they come out and sing a little snippet of a song, and it just feels very performative and like, oh, this is. But I think those moments where the show is incredibly powerful make it ultimately worth seeing. And especially with this cast. This entire cast was fantastic.
